Field notes · No. 2

Kyoto, one region a day

DJ, founderNovember 9, 20262 min read

Planning Kyoto with my partner last October started where every trip starts now: a group chat. Restaurant screenshots. A YouTube video called something like “Kyoto in autumn: a maple map.” A Google Maps pin neither of us could open on a laptop. And three separate messages that just said “bamboo grove??”

By week two the chat was mostly us asking each other where something was.

So I made a board called Kyoto and drew one region per day. Day 2 got a long name, “Higashiyama → Nishiki,” because that was the actual plan: temples early, food after.

The region did something the chat never could. It made the day finite. Once the box was full, it was full. If I wanted to add the bamboo grove, something had to move to Day 3, and that conversation took ten seconds instead of a whole evening.

Then I pasted the two links we kept sending each other. The maple-map video became a card with its thumbnail. Kiyomizu-dera became a place card with a little map. I drew an arrow from the video to the temple and labeled it “Watch before going.”

That arrow is my favorite thing on the board. It holds the reason. Six weeks later, standing in a hotel lobby at 6:40 a.m., I didn’t have to remember why the video mattered. The board remembered.

Here’s what surprised me. We skipped almost half the board. Rain on Day 3, a long lunch on Day 4 that turned into the best afternoon of the trip. In the chat, skipping things felt like failing the plan. On the board it felt like editing. The regions were still there, and we just picked the parts that held up.

If you’re planning something right now, try one region per day. Name each one the way you’d say it out loud. Put the reasons on the arrows. Then go, and let the board be wrong.
